subject: Zone claim -> host certificate handover protocol for private deployments
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@fincorp.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Fincorp Security <security@fincorp.com>
Date: 2028-03-28T16:12:00Z
Subject: Handing over zone claims and certs for private hosts

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. We're standing up a private deployment of Redwood in our us-west datacenter and want a straightforward, auditable protocol for handing zone claims and delivering host certificates for private FQDNs. Our security team needs to see a short runbook we can sign off on (scope: internal-only FQDNs, split DNS, on-prem gateway termination).

Key asks from our side:
- A clear checklist for what we (FinCorp) must provide vs what Redwood will provision.
- An assertion method for FQDN ownership that doesn't require opening inbound ports (we prefer DNS-based or signed CSR exchange).
- How you want OCSP/CRL/OCSP stapling handled for private CAs or intermediates.
- Expected TTLs and rotation cadence for certificates in private zones.

Can you send a proposed protocol and a template we can fill with zone names and contacts?

Cheers,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Cloud Security, FinCorp
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@fincorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Handing over zone claims and certs for private hosts

Alice — thanks for the clear asks. Attached are two artifacts to start: a compact zone-claim handoff template (CSV) and a CSR handoff checklist (MD). Summary of the proposed high-level protocol follows; details are in the attachments and the internal playbook link I included in metadata.

Proposed protocol (high level):
1) Zone claim record: customer provides a CSV with FQDN, intended resolver IPs (if split DNS), authoritative contact, and desired cert TTL/rotation window. (See zone-claim-handoff-template.csv)
2) Ownership proof: for on-prem/split-DNS setups we prefer a signed CSR exchange. Customer generates CSRs for each FQDN, signs them with their on-prem key, and sends via encrypted transfer (SFTP/DocuSign payload) — this avoids opening inbound ports. If customer cannot generate CSRs, we can issue a DNS TXT challenge for the private zone if the customer's DNS admin can create the TXT record in the split zone.
3) CA/chain selection: Redwood will sign with a customer-isolated intermediate (where requested) or our managed intermediate. For customer-managed intermediates we will ingest the intermediate certificate and configured OCSP responder URL.
4) OCSP/CRL: For private CAs we accept OCSP responder endpoints or periodic CRL exports; if neither is possible we'll provide a stapling-friendly policy and a private OCSP relay option (hosted within the customer's VPC) — see section 4 of the checklist.
5) Certificate distribution: Signed certs are delivered back via the agreed secure channel and can be pushed to customer bastions/vaults using the included distribution checklist. We also provide a pull-based delivery (CSR polling) for environments with strict egress controls.

Operational notes / gotchas:
- For split DNS, TTLs must align with your resolver's cache policy — recommend 300s for epoch changes.
- Pin the expected CA fingerprint in your clients/ingress to prevent accidental trust with a different intermediate during rollovers.
- If you need mutual TLS pinning, include client cert requirements in the CSV so we can coordinate CN/SAN policies.

Next steps: please complete the attached CSV and pick one of the ownership proof methods. If helpful we can run a 30-minute live handoff call before issuing any certs.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: zone-claim-handoff-template.csv (csv), csr-handoff-checklist.md (text)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-03-30T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Handing over zone claims and certs for private hosts — technical clarifications

Adding a few technical clarifications from an infra perspective:

- OCSP relay: our recommended pattern is to deploy a lightweight OCSP relay within the customer's VPC that proxies stapling requests to Redwood's OCSP responder over a mutual-TLS channel. This avoids exposing OCSP endpoints publicly and keeps latency predictable.

- CSR canonicalization: please ensure the CSR includes a SAN entry for any alternate service names; we'll reject certs where SANs are missing. Customers generating CSRs should use the tool in the checklist to validate SANs and key sizes (NIST 3072 or ECDSA P-256 recommended).

- Split DNS caveat: when using DNS TXT challenge for private zones, confirm that the authoritative DNS server used by your internal resolver will serve the TXT record world-accessible only via your internal network — we've seen misconfigurations where the challenge leaked to public DNS.

- Rollout and rollback: provide a canary host and a rollback FQDN mapping in the CSV so we can perform zero-downtime swaps in the event of cert issues.

I'll add examples to the internal playbook, but if you want them in the customer-facing checklist I can produce a trimmed version.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Engineering, Redwood Inference

Let's schedule a 30-minute working session next week (calendar invite to follow). If you want to fast-track an initial test cert we can do a single FQDN via CSR exchange after the CSV is received.
